rafi: Opening thread for quokka-embed v0.9 onboarding. Ran int4 per-tensor and saw a weird recall@5 regression concentrated on short Korean queries (<24 tok). anyone seen anisotropy-related failures at int4? :thinking:
sam: which eval split? short vs long?
rafi: short_korean_holdout (kr, ar, en). fp16 recall@5 on KR was 0.76. int4-per-tensor -> 0.62. int8-perchannel was 0.74. so int4 looks bad for KR only.
priya: wow big gap. cluster purity numbers? any manifold shifts?
rafi: UMAP + PCA whiten check: unwhitened PCA shows KR cluster condensation into fewer subclusters; average cosine similarity within KR rose by ~0.08, between-language separation reduced. mean L2 norm increased by ~0.09 for KR vectors.
zhao: int4 might be amplifying a few dominant dims causing anisotropy. Did you try isotropic scaling or post-quant centering?
rafi: tried simple L2 normalize post-quant (to unit), recall@5 improved from 0.62 -> 0.69 but still below fp16.
sam: try centroid matching: compute per-cohort mean offset fp16 - quant and subtract before KNN as a quick test.
rafi: queued centroid-correct + local reindex. command: `./evals/run_eval.sh --model quokka-v0.9 --quant int4-pertensor --dataset short_korean_holdout --knn hnsw --ef 200 --norm post_l2 --whiten false`
rafi: quant snippet:
```
quant:
  dtype: int4
  scheme: per_tensor
  symmetric: true
  clamp_percentile: 0.99
  calibrate_batches: 512
```
priya: clamp_percentile 0.99 may still clip tails badly. try 0.995 or enable outlier detection with per-dim scaling pre-quant.
zhao: also check tokenizer behavior for KR short queries. tokenization quirks can shift embedding scale if average token count small.
rafi: good point — token lengths match between fp16 and quant runs. variation negligible.
sam: any sample failures output? dump a few KR queries where nearest neighbor flips.
rafi: uploaded sample diff to s3: s3://redwood-evals/quokka/onboard/int4_kr_diffs.csv
priya: can you run an internal recall-by-topic? maybe certain topics (e.g., dates, named entities) are more sensitive because they live on specific dims.
rafi: running topic-binned recall now. also toggling PCA-whiten before quant (pre-whiten) to spread variance more evenly.
eval-bot: job queued job_id=2026_03_23_quokka_int4_kr_01, docs=32k, langs=[kr,ar,en], metrics=[recall@1,recall@5,cosine_gap,cluster_purity,mean_norm]
zhao: if pre-whiten helps, that suggests extreme eigendirections dominate and quant collapses them. We could add a lightweight pre-whiten step in the production pipeline for int4 models.
rafi: preliminary: pre-whiten + post-l2 norm recovered recall@5 to 0.73. still 0.03 shy of fp16.
sam: good recovery. remaining delta could be quant rounding bias; try small additive dither before quant or a bias-correct pass if our quant library supports it.
rafi: quant lib supports stochastic rounding? there's a flag `--stochastic`. I'll try that next.
priya: also consider using asymmetric int4 if symmetric is biting us on low mean dims.
eval-bot: follow-up: job_id=2026_03_23_quokka_int4_01 completed. results: kr_recall@5_fp16=0.76, kr_recall@5_int4_raw=0.62, kr_recall@5_int4_prewhiten_norm=0.73, overall_cosine_gap_reduced=0.05
rafi: thanks. I'll draft a short note recommending pre-whiten + post-normalize for int4 deployment in KR-heavy cohorts and flag int4-per-tensor as opt-in for non-KR routes. filing a follow-up ticket for biased-dim mitigation.
sam: add a smoke test in CI that runs the short_korean_holdout and fails onboarding if recall@5 drops >0.04 vs fp16.
priya: agree. also collect a small set of KR probe queries to monitor over time.
rafi: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
